pages.label: The ecosystem
pages.title: One platform. Every stage. Confidence across borders.
pages.description: Connect the people, products, evidence and decisions behind Halal trade. From supplier qualification to retail verification, the Amanah Halal Trust Ecosystem brings the whole journey into one coordinated operating model.

sections.title: What this means for your business
cards: Bring suppliers, ingredients, products, controls and audit actions into a clear market-readiness journey.
Follow custody, condition, shipment evidence and exceptions through the handoff to destination.
Review evidence in context, coordinate corrective action and preserve accountable decisions.
Inspect scoped disclosures and review purpose-bound trade evidence without exposing unrelated records.

sections.title: The complete platform, connected end to end
sections.text: Amanah is the operational workspace. AHTE provides the trust and assurance layer. GHSCL’s international operating model connects participating organizations across the journey. Together, the platform brings everyday coordination and supply-chain assurance into one coherent experience.
cards: Enterprise and facility profiles, products and SKUs, formulas and BOMs, suppliers, origin records, training and remediation from onboarding through continuous assurance.

Complete applicable Malaysian/JAKIM standards and instruments are mapped by applicability to requirements, controls, HCP/SCCP obligations and source-bound evidence; MS2400 is one applicable standards family, not the complete framework.
Sample identity, chain of custody, scientific evidence, guided observations, findings, CAPA and re-verification.
Connected representations of facilities, materials, batches, pallets, shipments, containers and seals; evidence graphs and integrity checks.
Monitoring, alerts, exception ownership, predictive analysis, Preemptive Strategy, escalation and recall coordination.
Warehouse and transport integration, Sinotrans logistics scope, telemetry, custody, port/customs events and destination receiving.
AHTE ⇄ Direct JAKIM API ⇄ JAKIM: evidence and status exchange subject to official activation; competent-issuer records remain independently owned.
Purpose-bound evidence packets, financing and underwriting case coordination, and approved digital-asset references.
Issuer-authorized product, batch and shipment disclosures for buyers, receiving teams and downstream stakeholders.
Projects, tasks, meetings, approvals, decisions, risks, documents, notifications and audit trails, organized by role and tenant.

sections.title: One journey from source to shelf
sections.text: Each stage carries its context forward: the object, the evidence, the responsible organization and the next decision. Teams work from a connected record instead of rebuilding the story at every handoff.

sections.title: Expertise across the complete journey
cards: Perak State Government halal-industry GLC operating locally and internationally within the project ecosystem.
International operating and digital-infrastructure vehicle for China → GCC orchestration and 24/7 Command Center operations.
Continuous standards, applicability, evidence, compliance, traceability, predictive analytics and trust intelligence.
Competent-authority system connected through the direct JAKIM API target. Review outcomes are recorded with their issuing organisation and supporting evidence.
Producers, suppliers, traceability systems, laboratories, manufacturers, warehouses, Sinotrans, ports and devices contribute attributable evidence.
Authorities, customs, importers, receiving warehouses, distributors, retailers and buyers apply destination controls and acceptance.

sections.title: A direct path for authority-connected assurance
sections.text: A direct connection keeps the authority workflow clear: AHTE ⇄ Direct JAKIM API ⇄ JAKIM. Formal certification approval or disapproval remains with authorised humans in the competent-authority workflow; PHC supports ecosystem development, assurance and institutional coordination but is not presented as the certification authority. AI does not certify. Official connections are activated under the relevant authority’s authorization.

sections.title: Shared confidence. Clear responsibilities.
sections.text: PHC, GHSCL, AHTE, laboratories, Sinotrans, port/customs authorities, GCC authorities, financiers, Takaful operators and competent Halal authorities retain distinct responsibilities. Evidence, monitoring and cryptographic integrity do not create another party's decision.

pages.label: Laboratory
pages.title: Analytical evidence with an unbroken sample chain.
pages.description: The laboratory workflow is designed for JAKIM-certified laboratories and their applicable scope. It binds test requirements, sample identity, collection, sealing, custody, receipt, method, QC, technical review, authorised sign-off and reports to the wider product and premises assurance case. A laboratory result is evidence; it is not halal certification.

sections.title: Certified laboratory workflow
sections.text: The laboratory workflow is designed for laboratories certified by JAKIM for their applicable scope. The platform links each authorised laboratory, operator, method and signatory record to the product and premises assurance journey.

sections.title: From test requirement to signed evidence
sections.text: Every analytical result remains bound to the sample, product/batch context, method, reviewer and provenance needed for accountable assessment.

sections.title: Continuous monitoring and certification decisions
cards: A result contributes analytical evidence to the assurance case.
Accredited scope, method controls and quality-control records determine how the result may be interpreted.
NOT_DETECTED ≠ HALAL. Certification records include their issuing organisation, scope and supporting evidence.

sections.title: LIMS and partner integration
sections.text: Laboratory systems connect through controlled adapters and canonical evidence objects. Serialization or anti-counterfeit platforms may support identity and traceability, but they do not replace a complete LIMS scientific workflow.

GNSS, seal, door, temperature/environment and vehicle telemetry connected to custody and route events.
Sample identity, sealing, scanning, instruments and workstation controls integrated with LIMS evidence.

sections.title: Device trust and offline continuity
sections.text: Offline operation preserves original evidence and sequence integrity; reconnecting never fabricates a successful external transaction.

sections.title: Procurement remains industry-specific
sections.text: Exact model, part number, regional certification, API/SDK, calibration, warranty, maintenance, lead time, spares and replacement availability are evaluated by industry and use case. Indicative hardware research is not a supplier quotation.

pages.label: API & interoperability
pages.title: Connect partner systems without redesigning AMANAH.
pages.description: AHTE keeps one canonical internal model while partner systems connect through governed adapters supporting modern APIs, legacy exchange patterns and controlled schema transformation.

sections.title: Supported integration patterns
cards: REST, SOAP and XML interfaces with versioning, idempotency, timeout and retry controls.
EDI, CSV, SFTP and batch exchange for systems that cannot expose modern APIs.
Queues, event streaming and webhooks for operational changes, telemetry and status propagation.

sections.title: Integration security and lifecycle
sections.text: OAuth/OIDC where appropriate, mTLS, PKI, device certificates, rate limits, secrets management, versioning, deprecation, UAT and rollback controls are applied without fabricating partner or authority activation.

sections.title: AI-assisted schema integration
sections.text: The integration copilot can compare partner schemas with the AMANAH canonical model, identify field gaps, propose mappings and test payloads, and run compatibility checks. Compliance-critical transformations require human approval and immutable mapping history.

pages.label: Cybersecurity
pages.title: Zero-trust controls for a cross-border evidence network.
pages.description: AMANAH cybersecurity protects identity, devices, APIs, evidence, workloads and operational continuity across manufacturers, laboratories, logistics, authorities and destination participants.

sections.title: Security control plane
cards: IAM, MFA, RBAC and ABAC where appropriate, least privilege and tenant isolation.
PKI, mTLS, TPM/HSM, device certificates, encryption, signed firmware and integrity proofs.
Secrets management, segmentation, API security, vulnerability management, SBOM and software supply-chain controls.
SIEM, alerting, incident response, evidence preservation and forensic readiness.

sections.title: Continuity under failure
sections.text: Cloud, API, authority-interface, partner, network, gateway, sensor, vehicle-connectivity and power outages are explicit operating states. An outage is never converted into fabricated success.

sections.title: Security preserves accountable roles
sections.text: Security and cryptographic integrity protect evidence and access; they do not create Halal certification, customs release, financing approval, Takaful approval or legal title.
